The summer experiment is a force multiplier, and we've been here numerous times and every single time we walk through the door. It is a different experience.... Not like your usual cocktail bars - in a bad way.
Jan 2026 • Couples
Overhyped bar - arguably the worst “top” bar in HCMC. They don’t even serve WATER. So basic.

This was my last bar in Vietnam and they didn’t do Vietnam any justice. Such a bad representation of the country., and I’ve been to more than 10 bars in the past 4 days. They all served water, great drinks, and great hospitality,
All the top bars i went to -
Hanoi:
Hafflington, Hudson Rooms, Track 61, Nê, Use Bar, Workshop 14,

HCMC: 
The Pi, Engima Mansion, Hybrid, Stir
- all of them were MUCH BETTER and at the very least - served water, which is a basic expectation of any GOOD bar.

And all of them I got to really connect with the bartenders and even add them as friends on instagram — here was the only only one I felt like I could not because the staff were very robotic and don’t have any personal touch. They didn’t even ask for our names even when I asked for theirs (which I normally do when I go bars!)

I spent more than 1 million by myself and they didn’t even have the decency to provide water???

I eventually paid for the glass of water and even paid more for it and they didn’t give any change or official receipt - I think that’s against consumer protection laws but I didn’t have time to argue anymore.

This is such an absurd and overhyped bar. Do not come here: worst in HCMC. Hospitality was super bad and mid.

Honestly, I don’t want to come back to HCMC just because of this.

Try Bees on Your Knees & Diggin' That Soursop
Sep 2025 • Friends
My friend & I tried 5 cocktails: (1) Pomelo's Senorita, (2) Bee on Your Knees, (3) Diggin' That Soursop, (4) On Cloud 9 and (5) Bounty Hunter. (1) was not exactly noteworthy. (2) with its chamomile flavour and polaroid photo moment was a winner. (3) tasted more of black tea than soursop, but despite its unassuming presentation (we mistook it for a glass of ice water), was lovely. (4) was literally over the top with its foam, but was less impressive in terms of taste - it was mostly lavender and no earl grey. (5) was the most expensive, but its ingredient description turned out to be more sophisticated than it actually was. We also had the prawn fritters, which was tasty and fresh. Loved the vibes overall and staff were friendly, but the cocktails were a bit of a hit and miss. Nevertheless, the strokes of genius shine through, and I would visit again the next time I'm in the city.

Review Highlights:

Inventive Cocktails: Summer Experiment is tucked away (up a slightly tired staircase) in what seems to be a residential building. But trust me, it’s worth the search! The lounge space exudes a cool vibe, and their cocktails are extremely inventive. They play with a wide variety of spirits, fruits, flowers, and spices. Try the “Mule Met The Apricot” for a tangy, ginger-infused delight.
Hidden Gem: Like many bars and coffee shops in the city, Summer Experiment is discreetly hidden without clear signs. However, it gained recognition on the World’s Best 50 list, and now you know why! It’s just a 2-minute walk from… well, wherever you are.
Happy Hour: The happy hour prices are amazing, making it affordable for both tourists and locals. Friendly bartender Ethan and the service staff ensure you have a great time. Plus, they serve some of the rare gins alongside their creative cocktails.
Overall Verdict: If you’re up for an adventure in mixology, head to Summer Experiment. The combination of great drinks, good vibes, and reasonable prices makes it a must-visit spot in Ho Chi Minh City! 🍹🌟

Amazing. Nice cocktail and oysters. Good music!
Dec 2022 • Solo
I have noticed a lot of bars and coffee shops around the city are hidden in buildings with no clear signs. Not sure why! Had this not come up on World's Best 50, I would never have known! It was a 2 minute walk from my hotel. Located on the second floor (I think) of an old and horrible building! However, the bar is nice. Smaller than expected but cool. Limited seating at the bar, high tables inside or flat seats on the balcony. Huge drinks menu. You could page for hours! I had a non-alcoholic cocktail which was so good and oysters with mignonette sauce. Divine. Couldn't fault. Their snack food menu is also nice. Perfect end to 2022. I stopped by early for Happy Hour when it was very quiet and it just opened. Staff were pleasant and friendly. They speak English. Fabulous music. Clean. My negatives. It was early, they were not busy. I was seated at the bar and told all other areas reserved. Then after 5 minutes, I was told I could have a high seat proper table! Silly. I wasn't planning to stay long. I just wanted a drink and a snack. I asked for a glass of water and was told I had to pay for a bottle. They could have just given me a glass of tap water! Would recommend otherwise. Cool atmosphere. Nice music. Loved my cocktail and oysters. I can see why it was in the World's 50 Best!

Lovely bar, but dead
Nov 2022
Interesting place, through an alley way and up a flight of stairs in what looked like an apartment block. Could do with better signage, as it wasn't immediately clear if I had arrived at the destination, as there was big door closed, that was not open. How very welcoming! I was about to walk away and give up but one of the staff peeped out and let me in.... Maybe it is too cool for customers?

Inside though, the decor is fantastic, a lovely looking bar, well stocked and with a high amount of alcohol of all types for sale. The lighting is just perfect and they have set the right mood for the bar. The view from the balcony is good too. 

The menu is very colourful and informative and they put a lot of work into it. I ordered an Apricot Vodka shot and also went for some Absinthe, my first time trying the fairy goblin. Both drinks were served well, although the lad doing the bar tending was a bit dim, glasses on the back of the head for some reason. I like professionals to pour me my hard liquor, not young kids. A bit of a mockery there. No interaction or chat about the drinks too......which considering I was the only customer wasn't very good. 

Still though, the waiting staff were very friendly and made some good chat.
I was the only customer there on a Saturday midday, which might say a lot, in a big city!

As for the drinks, yeah they were ok, presented well and with a bang and a flash, but not much taste really.... two shots came to about 12 Euros, which was as you'd expect back home perhaps. 

Lovely bar, but dead......

Eternal Summer
Jan 2020
Summer Experiment is a bit hard to find. Through a non-descript entryway, and up a few flight of stairs. Your intrepidness will be rewarded with a beautiful hidden cocktail bar. One of the few in Saigon that does not allow smoking inside (smoking is permitted on their outdoor balcony). This is a huge welcome for a non-smoker like me who miss the no smoking policy in California.

Summer Experiment is the new sister bar of the well attended Layla on Động Du, only more intimate and laid back. And like its sister, the cocktails really shine here. Delicious, luscious ice (yes, I said luscious ice), and gorgeous glassware. The staff is friendly, and the manager knowledgeable. The drinks are reasonably priced, a mixture of whimsical new concoctions and old stalwarts, and a very economical happy hour drink list. They have food on the menu, albeit small bar bites, so don’t come here with a full appetite. The food is not intended to be a full meal but rather a gustatory accompaniment to the star of the show, the cocktails.

The only reason I don’t give Summer Experiment 5-stars is because of their horribly heavy and exceedingly uncomfortable table chairs. High chairs that must weigh in excess of 20kg, and have a shallow seating depth that would even make a 5-year old whelp. These chairs make me yearn longingly for the tiny red plastic chairs that inhabit every sidewalk of Saigon. I’m a 5’ 8”, 155lbs Asian guy. I can’t imagine what torture the chairs must feel like for my larger American brethren.

But aside from my seating rant, Summer Experiment really is a wonderful addition to the Saigon cocktail scene. A must visit if you are looking for a chill and delicious cocktail experience.
